name: Philosophy
title: Philosopher / Ethics Consultant
intro: Philosophy is the systematic study of fundamental questions about existence, knowledge, ethics, and reasoning. Professionals apply rigorous analytical thinking to academic research, public ethics advisory, and interdisciplinary consulting.
whoShouldPursue: Strong inclination toward abstract reasoning and fundamental questions about knowledge and morality
Enjoys constructing and deconstructing arguments through logical analysis
Comfortable with long-form reading, writing, and sustained independent thought
Interested in applying ethical frameworks to real-world policy and technology challenges
eligibility: Bachelor's degree in Philosophy or a related humanities discipline
Master's or M.Phil. in Philosophy for academic and research positions
PhD required for university-level teaching and independent research
NET/SET qualification preferred for permanent academic roles in India
workDesc: Researching philosophical problems, writing papers and books, teaching undergraduates, and advising organisations on ethical questions in technology, healthcare, or public policy.
workExamples: Teaching undergraduate and postgraduate philosophy courses at a college or university
Conducting and publishing peer-reviewed research on ethics, epistemology, or metaphysics
Advising tech companies or government bodies on AI ethics and data privacy frameworks
futureOutlook: Growing demand for ethics consultants in AI, biotech, and data governance will create new non-academic career avenues for philosophy graduates.

name: Linguistics
title: Linguist / Language Scientist
intro: Linguistics is the scientific study of language structure, acquisition, and use across cultures and communities. Professionals analyse phonetics, syntax, semantics, and sociolinguistic patterns in research, technology, and language preservation roles.
whoShouldPursue: Fascinated by how languages are structured, learned, and evolve over time
Strong aptitude for pattern recognition and systematic analysis
Interested in both human cognition and computational applications of language
Comfortable working across disciplines like anthropology, psychology, and computer science
eligibility: Bachelor's degree in Linguistics or a language-related discipline
Master's in Linguistics or Computational Linguistics for specialised roles
PhD required for academic research and university positions
Coursework in phonetics, syntax, and statistics is highly valued
workDesc: Analysing language data, conducting fieldwork on understudied languages, developing natural language processing models, and teaching language structure courses.
workExamples: Conducting phonetic fieldwork to document an endangered language
Building annotation pipelines for natural language processing systems
Publishing research on syntactic variation across South Asian languages
futureOutlook: Demand is rising due to growth in NLP, voice assistants, multilingual AI, and government-led language documentation initiatives.

name: Cultural Studies
title: Cultural Studies Scholar / Cultural Analyst
intro: Cultural Studies examines how culture, media, power, and identity intersect in societies, drawing from humanities, social sciences, and critical theory. Professionals work as academics, media analysts, policy advisors, and cultural consultants.
whoShouldPursue: Deep interest in analysing media, popular culture, and social power dynamics
Strong critical thinking and ability to interpret texts, films, and cultural artefacts
Comfortable with interdisciplinary approaches combining sociology, literature, and history
Passionate about social justice, identity politics, and cultural equity
eligibility: Bachelor's degree in Humanities, Social Sciences, or a related field
Master's in Cultural Studies, Media Studies, or Gender Studies for specialised roles
PhD required for academic and research-intensive careers
Prior coursework in sociology, literature, or anthropology is advantageous
workDesc: Analysing media representations, conducting research on identity and representation, teaching university courses, and advising organisations on cultural sensitivity and inclusive practices.
workExamples: Publishing research on representations of caste and gender in Indian cinema
Teaching undergraduate courses on postcolonial theory and media criticism
Advising NGOs on culturally sensitive program design for marginalised communities
futureOutlook: The expanding media landscape and growing focus on cultural representation will sustain demand across academia, media analysis, and cultural consulting.

name: Museum Studies and Curatorship
title: Museum Curator / Heritage Professional
intro: Museum Studies and Curatorship involves the professional management of cultural collections, exhibitions, and heritage sites. Curators research, preserve, and interpret artefacts to educate the public and preserve cultural memory.
whoShouldPursue: Passionate about art, history, archaeology, or material culture
Strong organisational skills and attention to detail in documentation
Excellent written and verbal communication for exhibit interpretation
Enjoys combining research, aesthetics, and public engagement
eligibility: Bachelor's degree in History, Archaeology, Fine Arts, or a related humanities field
Master's in Museum Studies, Curatorial Studies, or Art History preferred
Internships or volunteer experience at museums, galleries, or heritage sites
Knowledge of conservation techniques and collection management systems
workDesc: Managing museum collections, researching artefacts, designing exhibitions, writing catalogues, liaising with donors, and overseeing preservation standards.
workExamples: Researching provenance of a Mughal miniature painting collection
Designing and installing a temporary exhibition on tribal art forms
Cataloguing and digitising a museum's archival photographic collection
futureOutlook: India's expanding museum sector and government heritage preservation initiatives will create steady demand for trained curatorial professionals.

name: Archaeology
title: Field Archaeologist / Heritage Excavation Specialist
intro: Field Archaeology involves the systematic excavation, analysis, and interpretation of material remains to reconstruct past human activity. Unlike purely academic history, this career centres on hands-on fieldwork, site excavation, and heritage management.
whoShouldPursue: Physically fit and comfortable working outdoors in rugged field conditions
Strong spatial reasoning and ability to document and map excavation layers
Fascinated by ancient civilisations and material culture
Patient and methodical with meticulous recording and classification work
eligibility: Bachelor's in History or Archaeology with coursework in archaeology
Postgraduate Diploma in Archaeology for professional field roles (ASI and state departments)
Master's or PhD for senior research and project leadership positions
Field training in excavation techniques, survey methods, and artefact handling
workDesc: Conducting excavation campaigns, analysing recovered artefacts, preparing site reports, and working with government agencies to protect and manage heritage sites.
workExamples: Leading a seasonal excavation at a Harappan settlement in Gujarat
Conducting surface survey and pottery analysis at a newly discovered megalithic site
Preparing conservation management plans for an ASI-protected monument
futureOutlook: Government investment in heritage preservation and expanding archaeology degree programmes will maintain steady, though competitive, demand for field professionals.
deg: PG Diploma in Archaeology for field roles

pathways.degree: PG Diploma in Archaeology  for field roles

name: Archival Studies
title: Archivist / Records Management Specialist
intro: Archival Studies focuses on the collection, preservation, organisation, and access of historical records and documents. Archivists ensure that institutional and cultural memory is systematically maintained for research and legal purposes.
whoShouldPursue: Extremely detail-oriented with strong organisational instincts
Comfortable working independently with large volumes of documentary material
Interested in history, information science, and cultural preservation
Prefers a structured, methodical work environment with minimal disruption
eligibility: Bachelor's degree in History, Library Science, or a related humanities discipline
Master's in Archival Studies, Library Science, or Information Management
M.Lib qualification is highly relevant for library-adjacent archival roles
Familiarity with cataloguing standards, metadata schemas, and digital preservation
workDesc: Appraising, acquiring, organising, and preserving collections of records, manuscripts, and digital files while providing access to researchers and the public.
workExamples: Appraising and accessioning a donated collection of 20th-century Indian political correspondence
Digitising fragile historical manuscripts using conservation-grade scanning equipment
Creating finding aids and metadata records for a state government archive
futureOutlook: Digitisation mandates and open-access initiatives are creating new roles, but overall growth remains steady and competitive.

name: Development Studies
title: Development Professional / Social Policy Analyst
intro: Development Studies examines the social, economic, and political dimensions of poverty, inequality, and progress in the Global South. Professionals work across government, NGOs, and international organisations to design and evaluate interventions that improve livelihoods.
whoShouldPursue: Deep commitment to social justice, poverty reduction, and equitable development
Strong analytical and research skills applied to real-world social problems
Comfortable working in multicultural and cross-disciplinary teams
Willingness to work in challenging field environments across rural and urban India
eligibility: Bachelor's degree in Social Sciences, Humanities, or related disciplines
Master's in Development Studies, Public Policy, or Social Work for professional roles
Fieldwork experience with NGOs or government programmes is highly valued
Coursework in economics, sociology, or statistics strengthens candidacy
workDesc: Designing and monitoring social programmes, conducting impact assessments, analysing policy, and liaising between communities, governments, and funding agencies.
workExamples: Evaluating the impact of a rural livelihood programme across three Indian states
Writing grant proposals and donor reports for a women's empowerment initiative
Analysing government policy data on education access in tribal districts
futureOutlook: Sustainable Development Goals and government welfare expansion will sustain strong demand for trained development professionals across sectors.

name: International Relations
title: International Relations Analyst / Foreign Policy Specialist
intro: International Relations studies the interactions between nations, international organisations, and global governance systems. Professionals analyse foreign policy, diplomatic strategy, and geopolitical dynamics in government, think tanks, and multinational settings.
whoShouldPursue: Strong interest in global geopolitics, diplomacy, and international law
Excellent analytical and writing skills with ability to synthesise complex information
Comfortable with ambiguity and rapidly shifting political landscapes
Multilingual abilities and cross-cultural sensitivity are valued assets
eligibility: Bachelor's degree in Political Science, International Relations, or History
Master's in International Relations, Strategic Studies, or Public Policy preferred
Competitive examinations (UPSC, Civil Services) are a common entry route into government IR roles
PhD or M.Phil for academic and research-focused careers
workDesc: Monitoring and interpreting global political events, drafting policy briefs, conducting diplomatic research, and advising government or organisational leadership on international strategy.
workExamples: Writing a policy brief on India's trade relations with ASEAN nations for a think tank
Analysing voting patterns and resolutions at the United Nations General Assembly
Conducting research on South Asian security dynamics for an academic journal
topIndustries: Ministry of External Affairs and Government
futureOutlook: India's growing global stature and expanding diplomatic footprint will create increasing demand for IR professionals in both government and private sectors.
tech: policy brief and white paper writing

name: Instructional Design
title: Instructional Designer / E-Learning Course Architect
intro: Instructional Design is the systematic process of creating effective learning experiences by applying educational theory, cognitive science, and multimedia design. Professionals architect courses, curricula, and learning modules for digital and blended environments.
whoShouldPursue: Strong blend of creativity and systematic thinking applied to education
Excellent writing and visual communication skills for content development
Interested in how people learn and how to optimise educational outcomes
Comfortable with e-learning authoring tools and learning management systems
eligibility: Bachelor's degree in Education, Humanities, or a related field
Master's in Education, Instructional Design, or Educational Technology preferred
Proficiency with e-learning tools (Articulate, Captivate, or similar)
Knowledge of learning theories, assessment design, and UX principles
workDesc: Analysing learning needs, designing course structures, developing multimedia content, and evaluating programme effectiveness in collaboration with subject-matter experts.
workExamples: Designing a six-module online certificate course on data literacy for government employees
Building interactive branching scenarios for a corporate compliance training programme
Conducting learner analysis and iterating course content based on completion and assessment data
futureOutlook: India's booming EdTech sector, online programme mandates, and corporate upskilling budgets will drive sustained high demand for skilled instructional designers.
